text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Liberal FDP pushes for early abolition of solidarity surcharge, Kohl aide Schaeuble says not before year 2000
- FDP sets out education reform programme
- Interior ministry wants to reinforce border guards on Polish border to stop illegal immigrants
- Capital trading tax not likely to be levied in east Germany
- Share prices fall at start of year
HANDELSBLATT
- IG Chemie chemical sector trade union says ready to talk to chancellor about "Alliance for Jobs" as long as negotiating rights of unions are protected
- Bourses get off to shaky start in New Year
- Rail prices to rise from April
- Handelsblatt leading indicator slips
- FDP relaxed about criticism from CSU
- Kirch increases DSF sports television stake as Springer pulls out
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Interior ministry to reinforce border guards on Polish border to stop illegal immigrants
- FDP considers atmosphere in coalition good despite attacks from conservative CSU
- Rail prices to rise
- FDP calls for student fees and more testing in education
- President of DIHT German Chambers of Commerce, Stihl, says no new jobs will be created until growth reaches three percent
- Lufthansa faces formal caution from Cartel Office for abuse of monopoly position
- IWH institute says production in east Germany will not fall further
- Bundesbank drains 8.4 billion marks from market
DIE WELT
- FDP says atmosphere in coalition has improved again
- 3,500 holidaymakers stranded on North Sea island
- Opposition SPD wants lower taxes for average earners
- Unemployment benefit lower this year
- Economists agree economy will grow 2.5 percent this year
- President of DIHT German Chambers of Commerce, Stihl, says German industry becoming less competitive
- 1997 to see substantial progress towards major tax reform
